invariants.title: Snapshot and CDC boundary
invariants.normative_statement: Snapshot state is exactly at S and CDC contributes only positions in (S,F].
invariants.predicate: for every CDC position p: S < p <= F
assumptions: S and F use the same source-position kind
invariants.minimal_counterexample: Position 100 is applied as CDC after snapshot S=100.
false_positive_risks: A forged source position can satisfy the interval.
false_negative_risks: Non-total native positions require a richer adapter comparator.
invariants.proves: Bounded interval membership for canonical positions.
invariants.does_not_prove: DMS captured every native log record.
invalidation_conditions: Boundary convention or position comparator changes.

invariants.title: Contiguous frontier chain
invariants.normative_statement: Every applied interval begins at the previously committed frontier with no gap or overlap.
invariants.predicate: for ordered intervals i: i.end == next.start
assumptions: Intervals share one generation and position kind.
false_positive_risks: Continuous declared intervals can still hide source omissions.
false_negative_risks: Equivalent vendor frontier encodings may require normalization.

invariants.title: Deterministic total order
invariants.normative_statement: Equivalent immutable inputs produce one unique source-consistent event order.
invariants.predicate: order keys are strictly increasing and unique
assumptions: Transaction and event sequences are authentic.
invariants.positive_example: Equal positions with event sequences 0 then 1 pass.
invariants.minimal_counterexample: Two events share position and both sequence values.
false_positive_risks: Fabricated sequence values can appear unique.
false_negative_risks: A vendor-specific tie breaker may not fit v1.
invariants.proves: Uniqueness and monotonicity of canonical order keys.
invariants.does_not_prove: Managed transport preserved native transaction order.

invariants.title: Identical replay idempotency
invariants.normative_statement: Reapplying identical immutable input leaves logical target state unchanged.
invariants.predicate: logical digest before replay equals logical digest after replay
assumptions: The replay identity and payload digest are verified first.
invariants.positive_example: An identical transaction replay preserves the state digest.
invariants.minimal_counterexample: Replay increments a value a second time.
false_negative_risks: Benign metadata-only changes can alter an incorrectly scoped digest.
invariants.proves: Logical digest stability for the bounded replay.

invariants.title: Replay conflict rejection
invariants.normative_statement: One immutable event or transaction identity cannot bind to two payload digests.
invariants.predicate: same identity and different digest is rejected before mutation
assumptions: Identity and payload use separate canonical digest profiles.
invariants.positive_example: A changed payload for an existing event ID is rejected.
invariants.minimal_counterexample: The changed payload overwrites the prior event silently.
false_positive_risks: Incorrect identity scope can classify distinct events as conflicts.
false_negative_risks: Excluded semantic fields can hide a conflict.
invariants.proves: The supplied conflict was not applied.
invalidation_conditions: Replay identity or payload digest profile changes.

invariants.title: Checkpoint and target commit coupling
invariants.normative_statement: A source frontier advances only with a matching durable target commit receipt.
invariants.predicate: checkpoint <= durable target frontier and receipt identity matches
assumptions: Target commit durability is independently established.
invariants.positive_example: Checkpoint 110 binds the durable commit ending at 110.
invariants.minimal_counterexample: Checkpoint 111 is stored while target durability ends at 110.
false_positive_risks: A forged commit receipt can satisfy the predicate.
false_negative_risks: Equivalent target commit aliases can be rejected.
invariants.proves: Bounded numeric frontier and receipt coupling.

invariants.title: Failure atomicity
invariants.normative_statement: A failed apply is invisible or deterministically recoverable without double application.
invariants.predicate: visible pre-state equals failure state, or recovery completes without double apply
assumptions: Visible state and replay effects are included in the digest.
invariants.positive_example: Injected pre-commit failure rolls back all mutations.
invariants.minimal_counterexample: A row is visible but its transaction receipt is absent.
false_positive_risks: Unobserved side effects can lie outside the state digest.
false_negative_risks: Equivalent recovered metadata may differ nonsemantically.

invariants.title: Delete and tombstone correctness
invariants.normative_statement: A delete removes active state, preserves auditable lineage, and participates in reconciliation.
invariants.predicate: row absent and tombstone present and reconciliation includes deletion
assumptions: A usable canonical primary key is present.
invariants.positive_example: Deleted row is absent and its tombstone remains auditable.
invariants.minimal_counterexample: Row disappears with no tombstone or reconciliation lineage.
false_positive_risks: A tombstone may reference the wrong source event.
false_negative_risks: A valid alternative retention representation may differ.
invariants.does_not_prove: Managed table retention and compaction behavior.

invariants.title: Schema safety and quarantine
invariants.normative_statement: Unknown or incompatible source contracts are quarantined before candidate mutation or publication.
invariants.predicate: incompatible data never reaches active state and is quarantined
assumptions: Exact source contract ID, version, and digest are available.
invariants.positive_example: A digest mismatch is quarantined before apply.
invariants.minimal_counterexample: An unknown contract mutates the candidate before rejection.
false_positive_risks: A registry can misclassify an incompatible change.
false_negative_risks: A compatible unregistered contract is conservatively quarantined.

invariants.title: Generation isolation
invariants.normative_statement: Candidate writes cannot mutate the consumer-visible active generation.
invariants.predicate: a write aimed at active generation is rejected unless it is outside migration flow
assumptions: Generation IDs identify physically isolated candidate namespaces.
invariants.positive_example: Candidate gen-2 write leaves active gen-1 unchanged.
invariants.minimal_counterexample: Migration apply writes directly into active gen-1.
false_positive_risks: Logical IDs may alias one physical location.
false_negative_risks: A safe non-migration maintenance write can be rejected by the bounded case.

invariants.title: Proof before publication
invariants.normative_statement: Publication requires all eight current, passing, same-boundary proof gates.
invariants.predicate: exact required gate set, all PASS, one boundary digest, one input revision
assumptions: Gate inputs and producers are integrity-bound.
invariants.positive_example: All eight gates pass for one generation/frontier/schema revision.
false_positive_risks: A semantically weak gate can still report PASS.
false_negative_risks: A renamed but equivalent gate is rejected until contract evolution.
invariants.proves: Proof-set completeness, pass state, freshness, and boundary equality.
invariants.does_not_prove: Each managed gate implementation is correct.
invalidation_conditions: Required gate set or freshness model changes.

invariants.title: Single-publisher compare and swap
invariants.normative_statement: At most one writer succeeds for one expected pointer revision.
invariants.predicate: success count <= 1 and expected revision is enforced
assumptions: All publishers use the same linearizable pointer primitive.
invariants.positive_example: Two writers race at revision 4 and exactly one advances to 5.
invariants.minimal_counterexample: Both writers report success for revision 4.
false_positive_risks: A non-linearizable store can violate the modeled primitive.
false_negative_risks: Idempotent duplicate success reporting can require richer modeling.
invariants.proves: The recorded schedule has no more than one success.

invariants.title: Stale writer rejection
invariants.normative_statement: A stale expected revision cannot mutate the active pointer.
invariants.predicate: stale write is rejected and pointer remains unchanged
assumptions: The observed pointer snapshot is captured before and after the attempt.
invariants.positive_example: Expected revision 3 against current 4 rejects without mutation.
false_positive_risks: A hidden side effect can occur outside the pointer snapshot.
false_negative_risks: Retry metadata can change while the pointer remains safe.
invariants.proves: Pointer immutability for the stale attempt.

invariants.title: Replay determinism
invariants.normative_statement: Equivalent immutable inputs yield identical logical-state and proof digests.
invariants.predicate: first and second logical digests match and first and second proof digests match
assumptions: Clock, locale, seed, order, versions, and volatile fields are controlled.
invariants.positive_example: Two clean runs produce byte-identical semantic reports.
invariants.minimal_counterexample: Input map order changes the proof digest.
false_positive_risks: Both runs can repeat the same deterministic bug.
false_negative_risks: Unexcluded harmless provenance can alter bytes.
invariants.proves: Two bounded executions agree on semantic digests.
invariants.does_not_prove: All platforms or dependency versions agree.
invalidation_conditions: Canonicalization, dependency, or proof-input scope changes.

invariants.title: Rollback eligibility and auditability
invariants.normative_statement: Rollback targets only a retained, readable, proven generation and records the decision.
invariants.predicate: target is proven, retained, readable, and decision is auditable
assumptions: Readability and retention probes are current for the decision revision.
invariants.positive_example: A retained proven generation is republished with a reason and new revision.
invariants.minimal_counterexample: Rollback targets a retired unreadable generation.
false_positive_risks: A stale readability claim can pass.
false_negative_risks: Emergency authority models may require a future contract version.
invariants.proves: All four eligibility facts are true in the supplied case.
invariants.does_not_prove: Managed consumer recovery or recovery time.
invalidation_conditions: Rollback eligibility or retention policy changes.

invariants.title: Evidence lineage integrity
invariants.normative_statement: Evidence binds verified artifact digests, commit, run, resources, references, labels, limitations, and producer versions.
invariants.predicate: artifact, commit, run, and reference verification all pass
assumptions: SHA-256 implementation and repository identity are trusted.
invariants.positive_example: Every manifest digest and reference resolves at the exact producer commit.
invariants.minimal_counterexample: One artifact byte changes without a manifest update.
false_positive_risks: A malicious producer can bind internally consistent false observations.
false_negative_risks: A safe relocation fails until the manifest is intentionally regenerated.
invariants.proves: Internal lineage and digest integrity for supplied evidence.
invariants.does_not_prove: The measured system behavior was correct.
invalidation_conditions: Evidence identity, digest, or repository-path rules change.
